title: Introducing Mastra Connect
summary: Your agents can now use Linear, Notion, Slack, and 20 other services with a single key.
body_markdown:
You can now connect providers like Linear, Notion, or Slack to your Mastra project with[Mastra Connect](https://mastra.ai/docs/mastra-platform/connect/overview) . Deploy agents that connect to your services from the CLI with a single auth flow.


note


Mastra Connect is in public beta. While in beta it's free to use on Mastra platform.


Every connection gives your agents and workflows ready-made tools, such as` linear_list_issues` ,` notion_create_page` , and` slack_post_message` .


You can manage credentials with` mastra connect add` , or from the dashboard, and the running app picks up the new tools within seconds.


Your browser does not support the video tag.


[Mastra](https://mastra.ai/ai-agent-framework) continues to support direct integrations via MCP, as well as integrations through[integration platforms](https://mastra.ai/blog/best-ai-agent-integration-platforms) like Composio, Nango, Arcade, and so on. But we wanted to build the simplest possible way to get started, giving an agent all the tools it needs to search real knowledge and take real action.


Today, Connect launches with 23 providers and almost 900 tools, plus 7 hosted MCP providers. More providers are coming, including Figma, GitLab, and Google Analytics.


If we connect to your provider but don't have the tool you need, you can use` credential()` to get the stored credential and call the provider's SDK directly.


## Get started


With a[Mastra platform](https://mastra.ai/docs/mastra-platform/overview) project set up, install Connect and the latest Mastra CLI:


Terminal


```text
npm   install   @mastra/connect
npm   install   -g   mastra@latest
```


note


Requires` @mastra/connect@1.0.0` and` @mastra/core@1.75.0` or later, added in[PR #26084](https://github.com/mastra-ai/mastra/pull/26084) .


Connect providers to your project. OAuth providers open a consent screen in the browser; API key providers prompt for the key in the terminal:


Terminal


```text
mastra   connect   add   linear   --project   your-project-name
mastra   connect   add   github   --project   your-project-name
mastra   connect   add   notion   --project   your-project-name
```


You can also add connections from the **Connect** page in the Mastra platform dashboard. The same page lists your connections and every request your agents make through them:


Your app reads connections with a platform access token and your project ID. Add both to` .env` :


.env


```text
MASTRA_PLATFORM_ACCESS_TOKEN  =  your-token
MASTRA_PROJECT_ID  =  your-project-id
```


When you deploy to Mastra platform, platform access token and your project ID are set for you.


Pass` tools()` to your agent. By default, the agent gets tools for every provider connected to the project; you can limit which providers and tools it uses.


This example limits the agent to Notion, Linear, GitHub, and Slack, and removes delete, archive, and merge tools:


src/mastra/agents/product-updates-agent.ts


```text
import   {   Agent   }   from   "  @mastra/core/agent  "  ;
import   {   Memory   }   from   "  @mastra/memory  "  ;
import   {   tools   }   from   "  @mastra/connect  "  ;


export   const   productUpdatesAgent   =   new   Agent  ({
id:   "  product-updates-agent  "  ,
name:   "  Mastra Product Updates  "  ,
instructions:   /* ... */  ,
model:   "  anthropic/claude-sonnet-5  "  ,
tools:   tools  ({
providers: [  "  notion  "  ,   "  linear  "  ,   "  github  "  ,   "  slack  "  ],
disallowTools: [  "  *_delete_*  "  ,   "  *_archive_*  "  ,   "  github_merge_pull_request  "  ]
}),
memory:   new   Memory  ()
});
```


Tool entries accept` *` globs, and new connections show up in the running app without a redeploy.


## Channels


Connections can also put your agents in Slack, Discord, or Telegram. Pass` channels()` to the` Mastra` constructor and the platform supplies each channel's bot credential:


src/mastra/index.ts


```text
import   {   Mastra   }   from   "  @mastra/core/mastra  "  ;
import   {   channels   }   from   "  @mastra/connect  "  ;
import   {   productUpdatesAgent   }   from   "  ./agents/product-updates-agent  "  ;


export   const   mastra   =   new   Mastra  ({
agents: { productUpdatesAgent },
channels:   await   channels  ()
});
```


Discord and Telegram still need a bot created in the vendor's console before you connect it. See[Channels](https://mastra.ai/docs/mastra-platform/connect/channels) for setup steps per platform.


## Raw credentials


When Connect doesn't have a tool,` credential()` returns the stored credential so you can call the provider's SDK directly:


```text
import   {   credential   }   from   "  @mastra/connect  "  ;


const   cred   =   await   credential  (  "  c_yourconnectionid  "  );
const   token   =   cred.type   ===   "  oauth2  "   ?   cred.accessToken   :   cred.apiKey;
```


Requests made with a raw credential skip the platform proxy, so they aren't recorded on the platform.
